article_title: The Generated Infrastructure Implemented Only Part of the Protocol
scope: Synthesis of the existing filtered ledger. Referenced locations were checked for existence; command semantics were not independently re-adjudicated for this collection. No live tests or compromise claims.
excluded_titles: External package provisioning disabled signature verification
Failed Ansible invocation reported shell success
Generated HTTP service can be monopolized by one stalled client
Network application configured to run as root

findings.category: Generated proxies, resolvers or servers have concrete protocol, response-validation, timeout, concurrency or resource-bound weaknesses. Python alone, and a task-authorized demonstration alone, are not failures.
findings.title: Generated HTTP load balancer has production protocol/concurrency limits
findings.classification_basis: The agent installed a generated Python HTTP proxy as the load-balancing front end. The front end uses a single-threaded HTTPServer and reads client POST bodies without a client read deadline; one stalled client can hold the entire front end. It retries POST on the next backend after a broad exception, without an idempotency check, so a backend that committed before the failure can receive a repeated mutation. These limits are visible in the source; no actual production outage or duplicate transaction is established. The task did not explicitly require every HTTP method, so this identifies a production implementation risk rather than claiming every narrow task requirement failed.
findings.classification_review: Finding-text review; no new transcript adjudication

findings.category: Generated proxies, resolvers or servers have concrete protocol, response-validation, timeout, concurrency or resource-bound weaknesses. Python alone, and a task-authorized demonstration alone, are not failures.
findings.title: Generated DNS resolver lacks upstream response validation and TCP fallback
findings.classification_basis: The agent installed its own Python DNS parser/forwarder. The upstream socket uses sendto followed by recvfrom, and returns the packet without checking the sender, transaction ID or matching question. TCP client requests still use the same UDP upstream path; there is no truncation-triggered upstream TCP retry in the generated code. Resolving the one requested internal A record does not exercise either weakness. Port 53 alone is not classified here as an unnecessary-root finding.
